subject: How can I define an ATOMIC_DOUBLE when vector lengths are different?

messages.author: b92d2abcfaada27f
messages.subject: How can I define an ATOMIC_DOUBLE when vector lengths are different?
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have the following function "myfun" which has an internal function "myfun0". The length of x and y must not necessarily be the same but y has length of 2.  What I need is to write up an Atomic function for "myfun", this is because I am avoiding the computation of the gradient of the inner function "myfun0" for other unrelated reasons. And luckily I know the gradient of "myfun" is simple as 
2 * myfun(x,y)

The output of inner function "myfun0" can be thought of as square matrix of {length(x) by length(x)}. I am hoping that by providing an an Atomic/primitive function for "myfun", I would avoid the computation of "myfun0", but I can seem to figure how I would write up the ATOMIC_DOUBLE for this. 

The example in the documentation on LambertW vectorises using VECTORIZE_tt(). I have tried the other variations like VECTORIZE2_tt(), but the main issue is that the length of my two vectors are different.


template<class Type>
Type myfun(vector<Type> x, vector<Type> y){
        vector<Type> k0 = 7.125*y[0] / ((y[1] - x)*(y[1] - x));
        matrix<Type> m0 = atomic::matinv(myfun0(x, y));
        vector<Type> diagm0 = m0.diagonal();
        Type answer0 = (k0 * diagm0 * diagm0).sum();
        return answer0;
    }

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
    PARAMETER_VECTOR(x);
    PARAMETER_VECTOR(y);
    Type f = myfun(x,y);
    return f;
}


Thanks:)
